calls.headline: One-year bill yield hits 26.35%, highest since March 2024, as the dollar rises to 54.91
calls.body: The average yield on one-year treasury bills rose to 26.35% at Thursday's auction from 26.16% a week earlier, and the six-month yield to 25.74% from 25.36%; the central bank accepted EGP 87.2bn against a EGP 95bn target (Mubasher, Youlyou). Its dollar rate ended Thursday at EGP 54.77 buy and 54.91 sell, from 54.63 and 54.76. Futures price a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 as near certain, about 98% on CME's FedWatch (Gotrade, Coinpedia). The EGX30 fell 0.45% to 50,311.78 on EGP 6.58bn of turnover, but foreigners bought a net EGP 224.9m of shares while Egyptians sold 147.9m and Arabs 76.9m (Arab Finance, Masrawy).
calls.view: Egypt is paying more to keep foreign money as the Fed tightens, and taking less than it offered shows the central bank resisting a faster climb. That keeps the pound drifting, not breaking: the desk expects the dollar to stay below EGP 56.50 through December 17, with banks earning more on bills and developers paying more for credit. Foreign share buying on a down day is a small, steady vote for the market at these prices. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The central bank's dollar rate closes above EGP 56.50 before December 17, or the one-year yield jumps above 27% at the next auction.

calls.headline: Brent eases to $95.44 before OPEC+ as Saudi-Houthi strikes continue
calls.line: Oil near $95 keeps Egypt's import bill high into December, with a quota rollover already priced in.
calls.body: Brent settled 1.17% lower at $95.44 on Friday, still up 3.1% on the week. OPEC+ meets online on Sunday and is considering rolling current quotas into January, two delegates told Bloomberg (via Yahoo Finance), while some members dispute the new capacity figures behind 2027 targets (Japan Times). Saudi Arabia said it shot down a Houthi cruise missile aimed at Riyadh on Saturday, after strikes on Sanaa (AP).
calls.view: A rollover is priced in, so Sunday is unlikely to lower Egypt's fuel bill; the risk is upward, from attacks on Saudi energy sites such as the Jazan refinery. Dearer fuel and a weaker pound together raise import costs, one more reason the central bank holds on December 17. Low confidence on the oil level.
calls.wrong: Brent closes below $88 before the central bank's December 17 meeting.

calls.headline: Suez transits run 31% above last November as container lines return
calls.line: Canal dollars are recovering faster than the Houthi threat to Saudi ports is growing, for now.
calls.body: In the week to November 22, 318 ships of 30.1m dwt crossed the canal, 31% more than the weekly average of November 2025 though 28% below pre-crisis tonnage, and container capacity reached 984,782 TEU, 24% below pre-crisis levels (Lloyd's List Intelligence). The Suez Canal Authority put revenue at $593m in the first weeks of November against $295m a year earlier, and Maersk told President Sisi it will restore its full network through the canal within months (DNE Africa).
calls.view: A second dollar source is rebuilding beside foreign bill buying, which softens the pound's exposure to a Fed hike. The risk is the Red Sea itself: the Houthis claimed attacks on Jeddah and Jazan this week. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: Weekly Suez transits fall back below the November 2025 average, or a major line suspends canal sailings again.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction rises 3.5% to EGP 790 as OCI leaves Amsterdam
calls.line: The rebound undoes Wednesday's fall, but 97.2m new shares reach OCI's holders around December 8.
calls.body: Orascom Construction rose 3.5% to EGP 790.00 on Thursday, OCI's last day of trading in Amsterdam before it delists on Friday. The combination added 97,201,359 shares, lifting the count to 207.4m from 110.2m; NNS Holding and the Sawiris family hold about 78% of OCI, and the new shares are credited on or around December 8 (EnterpriseAM, Prop News Time).
calls.view: About a fifth of the new shares go to holders outside the Sawiris family, some of whom bought OCI for its Dutch listing and may sell Egyptian shares; that supply can cap the stock into mid-December. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The stock closes above EGP 830 before December 15.

calls.headline: Chipmakers lead Wall Street's best week since April 2025
calls.body: The S&P 500 rose 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.18% to 50,774.94 in Friday's half-day session, as Micron gained 7.6%, Marvell 7.3% and the chip index 4.7%; Nvidia ended only 0.8% higher (Reuters via Yahoo Finance). On the week the S&P 500 gained 5.6% and the Nasdaq 6.68%, and the Dow had its biggest weekly gain since October 2022 (CNBC via MLQ.ai). SanDisk rose 15.96%, Intel 5.4% to $57.40 and Broadcom 3.8% to $312.34.
calls.view: This is relief after the worst week since 2020, not a turn: the credit worries behind the selloff are unchanged, with Oracle still below its $116 offer price, volume was thin, and the Fed is set to tighten on December 9. The desk expects the Nasdaq to give back part of the week before the Fed. Low confidence: a strong Broadcom guide could extend the rally.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 25,000 before December 9.

calls.headline: A December hike is priced at about 98% as the dollar firms
calls.line: With the hike in prices, what the Fed signals for January moves stocks.
calls.body: Markets price a 98% chance of a quarter-point rise at the December 8–9 meeting, which would take the range to 4.00–4.25% (Barchart); CME's FedWatch showed 99.4% on Thursday (Invezz). The dollar index rose 0.37% on Friday after October's trade deficit came in at $149.5bn against $136.0bn expected, a 19-month high (Barchart), and the 10-year Treasury yield ended the week at 4.94%.
calls.view: The hike itself is no longer news; a statement that leaves January open would hit rate-sensitive stocks and help the dollar, while a signal of a pause would lift small caps and housing. The desk leans to the first, given growth revised to 4.3% and core PCE at 3.3%. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: Futures odds for December fall below 70%, or the 10-year closes below 4.50%.

calls.headline: Tesla rises 5.2% to $400 as SpaceX merger talks advance
calls.line: Deal talk, not deliveries, is setting Tesla's price, with no terms on the table.
calls.body: Tesla rose 5.2% to $400.00 on Friday, from $380.14 on Wednesday, after trading as high as $401.18 (AOL), as special committees of Tesla's and SpaceX's boards negotiate a possible all-stock merger (FXLeaders); the FT reported on November 23 that each company named five directors to the talks (MarketScreener). SpaceX trades below its $135 June offer price (FXLeaders).
calls.view: Without terms the stock is trading on hope: an all-stock deal would dilute Tesla's holders at a price no one has yet set, and Texas's incoming attorney general has promised scrutiny. The desk expects the gain to fade unless terms come out. Low confidence: one leak on terms could move it 10% either way.
calls.wrong: Tesla closes above $440 before any merger terms are announced.

calls.headline: Vertex falls 5.2% as the FDA delays its kidney drug to February
calls.line: A delay, not a rejection: the risk is a rival reaching the market first.
calls.body: The FDA moved its decision on povetacicept for IgA nephropathy from November 30 to as late as February 28, 2027, after classifying a late reply from Vertex as a major amendment (Tech Times, Medical Daily). Vertex fell 5.24% to $534.57 on Friday; Citi kept its Buy rating and $585 target, calling the delay "not thesis changing" (StockTwits via TradingView), and rival Vera Therapeutics rose about 14% (Medical Daily).
calls.view: Three months' delay costs Vertex little in value but hands Otsuka and Vera time in the same disease; the fall prices the delay, not a rejection. Low confidence.

view.headline: The IMF and Suez hold the dollar below EGP 56.50
view.body: The pound slipped 0.3% to 54.91 on Thursday as one-year bills rose to 26.35%, but the IMF staff deal, a canal earning double last year's dollars and record remittances should keep the dollar below EGP 56.50 through the December 17 meeting. The risk is a Fed that hikes and signals more: bills would then need to climb further to hold foreign money.
